chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him about emancipating the slave woman (al-nasama). So he said: Emancipate one who can make herself self-sufficient.

key_terms.أعتق: i'tiq: to emancipate, to free from slavery; a religiously meritorious act in Islamic law
key_terms.أغنى نفسه: aghna nafsahu: 'made himself/herself self-sufficient'; the criterion of financial self-sufficiency as a condition for preferential emancipation
key_terms.النسمة: al-nasama: literally 'soul/breath of life'; in jurisprudence refers to a living person, especially a slave — here specifically a slave woman to be emancipated

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on which slave should be emancipated first according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) was asked about the emancipation of a female slave (al-nasama). His ruling provides a jurisprudential criterion: when freeing a slave woman, one should prefer to emancipate those who are capable of supporting themselves financially. This reflects the broader Islamic concern that manumission be genuinely beneficial, not a means of abandoning the freed person to destitution. In the context of 2nd-century AH Kufa and Medina, where slavery was a social reality, this ruling guided how the faithful could fulfill the meritorious act of freeing slaves in the most beneficial way.
